headline: ChatGPT has reportedly been adding the real signatures of more than a dozen New Yorker cartoonists to fake cartoons it generates.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: older news re-dated; Nieman Lab reported it on 5 Oct 2026 and other outlets followed on 6 to 8 Oct, so Mashable's 12 Oct piece adds little that is new.
importance_line: What changed is that a chatbot is producing fake work carrying real artists' names, which hits working cartoonists first, then publishers such as Condé Nast negotiating AI licences, then OpenAI, but the evidence is viral examples gathered by Nieman Lab and OpenAI's reply does not address the cause.
source: Nieman Lab, as relayed by Mashable
summary: Nieman Lab reported on 5 Oct 2026, as relayed by Mashable on 12 Oct, that ChatGPT has repeatedly put the real signatures of more than a dozen New Yorker cartoonists on AI-made cartoon images without their permission or payment. The New Yorker says its publisher Condé Nast's 2024 deal with OpenAI did not allow training on its cartoons or use of its art in image generation, and OpenAI said it appreciates users "flagging bugs and unintended behavior"; ChatGPT now warns of a possible guardrail violation but still makes the images.
notes: Nieman Lab's page returned 403; text read on Mashable (https://mashable.com/tech/chatgpt-new-yorker-cartoon), which cites Nieman Lab as first reporter. Link kept on Nieman Lab as the original. Story first reported 5 Oct 2026 and widely covered 6 to 8 Oct.
